Subject: Post-call: Integration & Auth options for BankLytics POC

Hi Suresh — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned before the technical deep dive.

Summary of requirements we heard:
- POC will evaluate embeddings + reranker to improve search relevance across financial records.
- Strong constraint: no long-lived plaintext API keys stored in customer apps. Prefer short-lived tokens or service accounts issued via internal KMS/IdP.
- Audit & traceability: SecOps needs access to audit logs for token issuance and per-request metadata.
- Network: BankLytics expects either VPC peering or Private Deployment (we should confirm in the deep dive).

Open questions for the deep dive:
1) Do you have an existing OIDC provider for service accounts (Okta/ADFS/etc.) or would you prefer Redwood-managed service accounts with KMS integration?
2) Rotation cadence: you mentioned 30–90 day rotation in the call — can you confirm the enforced policy?
3) Which SDK languages are your engineers using (Python/Node/Go)?
4) Will embeddings be stored/used in your environment (reranker locally) or do you prefer them hosted in Redwood?

Attachments: network_diagram.png (image/png) — you referenced a diagram on the call; if you could upload your topology that would help Rishi prep. Also attaching our quick auth primer: redwood_sdk_auth_guide.pdf (see section 2 for recommended flows).

Proposed next steps:
- Technical deep dive (60 min) with Rishi — I’ll propose times below.
- Rishi will sketch an auth flow that supports short-lived JWTs, KMS-backed keys, and automatic rotation.
- Lauren will draft a high-level mutual action plan and required artifacts for procurement.

Available slots: Tue 02/17 10:00–11:00 PST, Wed 02/18 09:00–10:00 PST. Please let me know what works.

Thanks — Marissa

Subject: Re: Post-call: Integration & Auth options for BankLytics POC

Marissa — thanks for the summary. Confirming the priority and answering the questions you listed: 

- IdP: We use Okta (OIDC) for service accounts and prefer OIDC/OpenID Connect flows where possible.
- Rotation: SecOps enforces rotation every 30 days for service credentials; short-lived tokens (<= 1 hour) exchanged via a secure token service is preferred.
- SDKs: Backend services are primarily Node + a small Python ML service.
- Embeddings: We’d like embeddings to be stored in our environment if possible — reranker should be able to call Redwood for embedding generation and host vectors locally for rerank.

We don’t want any permanent API keys embedded in code or in containers. Ideally, we mint short-lived tokens from our internal token broker (Okta) and exchange for Redwood access tokens via a secure backend. We also need proof points for crypto/key storage — our audits will want KMS integrations and SOC2 evidence.

I attached the network diagram we referenced on the call (network_diagram.png). Happy to do the deep dive on Wed 02/18 09:00 PST.

Best,

Hi all — quick technical notes ahead of tomorrow’s session. High-level recommended approach that maps to your constraints:

1) Service account + short-lived tokens flow (recommended)
- BankLytics mints a signed JWT from Okta (service account credentials) -> backend exchanges JWT with Redwood Token Exchange endpoint -> Redwood issues an access token scoped to the requested model/route with a TTL (recommend 1h).
- Access token usage: tokens are not persisted by the client; they are kept in-memory by the backend and rotated automatically.

2) Key management / rotation
- We support KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) for encryption of persistent keys and for signing where needed.
- For audit we can surface token issuance logs and per-request metadata to CloudWatch/Stackdriver/your SIEM via our observability connectors.

3) SDK & routing
- Redwood SDK (Node/Python) includes an auth plugin to perform the token exchange against the Token Exchange endpoint and transparently refresh tokens.
- Routing: recommend a primary routing policy to your dedicated private region (if you go Private/Dedicated) with fallback to hosted models for elastic bursts — SDK can be configured with routing policy hooks.

4) Embeddings + rerank
- Suggested pattern: call Redwood Embeddings API for vector generation (short-lived access tokens), persist vectors in your local vector DB (we’ve seen customers use Milvus/FAISS). Reranker can call Redwood Rerank endpoints during query time or run a lightweight local model if latency tight.

Prep items for the deep dive (what I’ll bring):
- auth_flow_example.txt (simple JWT exchange sequence + example curl)
- snippets for Node SDK auth middleware (we’ll demo tomorrow)
- sample policy for routing and token TTL config

If you’re okay with that pattern I’ll create a prototype auth flow and push code samples to the shared Drive before the call.

Thanks — Rishi

Rishi/Marissa — couple quick questions before the deep dive: 
- Can Redwood surface token rotation events to our SIEM in near-real time (we need <5m latency for alerts)?
- Does Redwood support a push-based key rotation workflow (Redwood rotates keys and pushes new public keys to our KMS) or do you recommend our org control rotation and Redwood adapt?
- For audit: will we get request-level logs that include the agent/service-account id used in the request?

Also, on capacity: we require sub-100ms P50 for embedding generation for our realtime path — is Dedicated required to meet that, or can hosted with routing suffice?

Thanks,
BankLytics SecOps
secops@banklytics.com

Great questions — confirming the deep dive at Wed 02/18 09:00–10:00 PST (I’ve sent a calendar invite). Agenda below:

1) Auth flow overview: Rishi to demo JWT exchange + Token TTLs (15m)
2) KMS/rotation patterns and audit logs (15m)
3) Embeddings latency and routing (15m)
4) Mutual action plan & procurement next steps (15m)

Immediate answers to SecOps questions: 
- Token rotation events: yes — we can stream token issuance/rotation events to your SIEM via our observability connector. We’ll confirm exact latency <5m in the deep dive and capture any network requirements.
- Rotation orchestration: recommend customer-controlled rotation (you rotate keys in your KMS and Redwood pulls/validates public keys) for strongest auditability. We can also support push-based rotation for partners where customer cannot manage keys; we’ll discuss tradeoffs tomorrow.
- Request-level logs: yes — request logs include a service_account_id field, request_id, timestamp, model id, and route. Retention/PII settings are configurable.
- Latency: for consistently sub-100ms P50 on embeddings, Dedicated capacity in your region is the recommended path; we’ll show benchmark numbers and options for hosted-with-routing fallbacks tomorrow.

Pre-read: I uploaded the auth primer and Rishi’s auth_flow_example.txt to the shared Drive link above. If you can confirm any preferred IdP endpoints (OpenID metadata URL) ahead of the call it will speed the demo.

Action items before the call:
- BankLytics: share OpenID metadata URL + any network egress restrictions.
- Redwood (Rishi): prototype token exchange and Node SDK snippet; push to Drive.
- Lauren: draft procurement checklist and expected timeline.

See you tomorrow — Marissa
